title: A conditional applicability marker licenses a rule only under a stated context
summary: Test whether a recurring whole marks that a following operation/field applies only when a bounded preceding condition is met, rather than being an unconditional action, generic connector, or exception override. GDT269's same PAGE_HOST with q and bare renderings supplies a source-informed conditioning question, not semantic gold.

design.mechanism: A whole scopes over a precondition-to-applicability relation: the following rule is licensed only when the bounded condition holds.
design.unit: Complete candidate occurrences with an independently coded preceding condition, following rule/action field, and a matched no-marker default context.
design.contrast: candidate-bearing conditional applicability versus the same rule applied unconditionally or after a condition without the candidate; exception overrides and causal consequence are separate rivals.
design.prediction: The candidate should predict a stable interaction between the preceding condition and whether the following rule/action is licensed, with the rule absent or marked inapplicable when the condition fails; an unconditional wrapper/default predicts no condition-by-marker interaction.
design.falsifier: If the following rule occurs with equal authorization under failed and satisfied conditions, or the candidate only tracks record position/template while condition status adds no held interaction, the conditional-applicability hypothesis fails.
design.availability: Independent condition, applicability/license, and candidate-bound endpoint availability_unknown; GDT269 explicitly assigns no semantic operator or meaning.
design.related: Near IDEA000030 causal connector, IDEA000031 contrast marker, IDEA000032 coordination marker, and IDEA000034 exception override, but distinct in unit and falsifier: licensing an ordinary rule under a condition, not cause/consequence, opposition/list scope, or deliberate rule override.
design.countermodel: A renderer/template model can produce the same positive association if the candidate is simply an outer wrapper selected by PAGE_HOST or field position; GDT269's loss of strength under within-field-position conditioning is compatible with that model. Therefore a positional association alone cannot confirm conditional applicability.

source_evidence.quote:
This removes the simplest alternative that GDT267 merely compared different
host vocabularies on earlier and later records. The same opaque PAGE_HOST can
occur with q and bare rendering, and q remains earlier-associated within exact
page/host strata.
